items.question: Inspections cannot keep up with the number of ageing bridges
items.question_th: การตรวจสอบตามไม่ทันจำนวนสะพานที่อายุมากขึ้นทุกปี
items.credit_th: งานร่วมกับจุฬาลงกรณ์มหาวิทยาลัย
items.context: Visual inspection is slow, inconsistent between inspectors, and cannot reach every surface. Thailand's bridge stock is large and much of it is decades old.
items.approach: UAV surveys that deliver high-resolution imagery of the structure, and nonlinear finite-element analysis that turns the observed damage into a structural assessment. AI damage detection is being developed in the NRCT projects.
items.findings: On an RC bridge in service for more than seventy years, UAV imagery located the flexural-shear cracks precisely enough to compare them with the crack patterns from nonlinear finite-element analysis. The study hypothesized that the cracks came from fatigue under repeated loading, and showed the potential of UAV surveys to cut inspection time and cost.
items.limits: Image-based methods see surfaces. Internal defects, corrosion behind sound cover and prestressing losses still need non-destructive testing and sensors.

items.credit: Joint work with Chulalongkorn University and the Asian Institute of Technology.
items.question: The bridge on the drawings is not the bridge in the field
items.question_th: สะพานในแบบไม่ใช่สะพานในสนาม
items.credit_th: งานร่วมกับจุฬาลงกรณ์มหาวิทยาลัยและสถาบันเทคโนโลยีแห่งเอเชีย
items.context: Assessments are usually based on design drawings. After decades of service, geometry, stiffness and behaviour have all drifted from what was drawn.
items.approach: 3D LiDAR scanning for as-built geometry, ultrasonic pulse velocity for in-place stiffness, accelerometers and dynamic strain gauges under traffic, and a digital twin built on the as-is data rather than the as-designed data.
items.findings: For a balanced cantilever bridge, the point-cloud model exposed discrepancies between as-designed and as-built conditions; modal frequencies, mode shapes and neutral-axis depth extracted from the measurements agreed well with the as-is twin, so dynamic strain and neutral-axis parameters can serve as sensitive indicators of local damage.
items.limits: One structure and a baseline campaign. Long-term monitoring and repeated surveys are needed before change detection becomes routine.

items.credit: Joint work with Waseda University and Lehigh University, and on individual papers with Tongji University, Kanazawa Institute of Technology and Central Nippon Expressway. Builds on the director's doctoral research at Waseda University.
items.question: Corrosion is not uniform, so an average understates the risk
items.question_th: การกัดกร่อนไม่สม่ำเสมอ ค่าเฉลี่ยจึงประเมินความเสี่ยงต่ำเกินจริง
items.credit_th: งานร่วมกับ Waseda University และ Lehigh University และในบางบทความร่วมกับ Tongji University, Kanazawa Institute of Technology และ Central Nippon Expressway ต่อยอดจากงานวิจัยระดับปริญญาเอกของหัวหน้าศูนย์ที่ Waseda University
items.context: Chloride-induced corrosion varies along and across every bar. In prestressed beams, capacity is governed by the worst local loss, which an average measurement never shows.
items.approach: Corrosion measured along the bars and strands of RC and prestressed specimens; random-field models fitted to the measured spatial patterns; 3D nonlinear finite-element analysis of members with simulated corrosion.
items.findings: Transverse correlation of steel weight loss among multiple tensile bars was quantified experimentally and shown to change the failure probability of RC girders. In prestressed beams, capacity and ductility were governed by the maximum local weight loss of a single wire in the maximum-moment region, and prestress widened corrosion-induced cracks.
items.limits: Accelerated corrosion in laboratory specimens. Field corrosion is slower and its spatial statistics may differ.

items.credit: From the director's doctoral research at Waseda University, with colleagues at Lehigh University, Tokyo City University and Central Nippon Expressway.
items.question: How should an inspection change our confidence in a structure?
items.question_th: ผลการตรวจสอบควรเปลี่ยนความมั่นใจที่เรามีต่อโครงสร้างอย่างไร
items.credit_th: จากงานวิจัยระดับปริญญาเอกของหัวหน้าศูนย์ที่ Waseda University ร่วมกับนักวิจัยที่ Lehigh University, Tokyo City University และ Central Nippon Expressway
items.context: Inspections produce local observations, such as crack widths at a few points. Reliability estimates need to absorb them without pretending they describe the whole member.
items.approach: Random-field models of corrosion-related variables and a particle filter that updates them from spatially observed data, giving time-dependent reliability that reflects what was actually seen.
items.findings: In an example RC bridge girder updated from crack-width observations, the accuracy of the time-dependent reliability estimate improved as more locations were observed; the effect of the spacing between locations was also examined.
items.limits: Illustrative example on one member type. Linking the framework to routine inspection records is part of the flagship program.

items.question: From one bridge to a network: which structure, which repair, in what order?
items.question_th: จากสะพานแห่งเดียวสู่ทั้งโครงข่าย: โครงสร้างไหน ซ่อมอะไร และทำก่อนหลังอย่างไร
items.context: Budgets and engineers are limited. Decisions have to be made across hundreds of structures at once, on comparable data.
items.approach: Bridge Intelligence: the full chain from survey to decision on a pilot bridge, linked to network-level prioritization, with data standards that owner agencies can adopt, under the NRCT digital twin project started in 2026.
items.findings: In progress. Results will be reported here as they are published.
